source: Sztyber-Betley et al. (2025) Are Diagnostic Concepts Within the Reach of LLMs? (DX 2025)
finding: First paper to link LLM output to MBD concepts directly. LLMs were asked to build MSO sets, conflicts, then diagnoses (minimal hitting sets of minimal conflicts) for logic and arithmetic circuits. Ground truth came from the Fault Diagnosis Toolbox and a hitting set program.
numbers: Models: gpt-4o-mini (with code interpreter), o1-2024-12-17, o3-mini-2025-01-31. 4o-mini ran at temperature 0; o1 and o3-mini at reasoning effort high (dedicated approach) or medium. Each step was fed correct inputs from the previous step so step accuracy is measured alone. Exact per-model F1 values are only in figures, not in text.
quote: Diagnoses generation is the most computation-heavy task.
limits: Small custom circuit set (built by hand, so not in training data). Only component faults, all inputs and outputs measured. Exact scores not in text.
agent_relevance: A scaffold that splits diagnosis into model, conflicts, then hitting sets can be scored step by step. Our agent should hand the hitting-set step to code, not to the LLM.

source: Sztyber-Betley et al. (2025) Are Diagnostic Concepts Within the Reach of LLMs? (DX 2025) - diagnosis step
finding: Diagnosis (hitting set) generation by LLMs got clearly worse as the example got larger (more relations, more diagnoses). o3-mini did best on diagnoses; o1 best on conflicts and MSOs.
numbers: Authors report a clear decrease of F1 with number of relations and number of diagnoses (Figs 11, 12); o3-mini best (Fig 15); o1 best on conflict generation (Fig 14) and overall MSO (Fig 13).
quote: We observe a clear decrease in the performance with increasing complexity
limits: Precise F1 numbers not in text. Few examples. OpenAI models only.
agent_relevance: The hitting-set stage is where LLMs break first as the suspect space grows. Supports a code tool for the search over suspects.

source: Sztyber-Betley et al. (2025) Are Diagnostic Concepts Within the Reach of LLMs? (DX 2025) - conflicts with zero inconsistency
finding: Conflict generation looked better with more complexity only because of a floor effect: models did badly when the true number of conflicts was zero (no inconsistency), i.e. they invented conflicts.
numbers: Trend lines rise with complexity, which the authors attribute to poor scores in the zero-conflict case. Empty-vs-empty was scored precision=recall=1 by convention.
limits: Interpretation by authors; no count given in text.
agent_relevance: Hallucinated conflicts would add false hitting-set constraints and exclude the true diagnosis. The agent should verify each conflict by a check before use.

source: Sztyber-Betley et al. (2025) Are Diagnostic Concepts Within the Reach of LLMs? (DX 2025) - prompt knowledge
finding: Adding domain knowledge to the prompt did not help. The Dedicated prompt (rich domain knowledge) and the Broad prompt gave similar MSO results. Giving the correct incidence matrix as input also did not change MSO results much.
numbers: Dedicated vs Broad: similar across all three models. Footnote: gpt-4o and gpt-4o-mini had accuracy close to zero on unseen examples without a code interpreter.
quote: The performance of the Dedicated and Broad Approach is similar despite much more domain knowledge
limits: Qualitative statement; aggregated over two approaches.
agent_relevance: Prompt detail is a weak lever here; tool use and a reasoning model matter more.

source: Sztyber-Betley et al. (2025) Are Diagnostic Concepts Within the Reach of LLMs? (DX 2025) - incidence matrix
finding: The simplest step (equation-variable incidence matrix) was solved perfectly by o1 and o3-mini. 4o-mini added known variables and fault variables, giving poor scores.
numbers: o1 and o3-mini: perfect accuracy on incidence matrices. 4o-mini: extra variables included.
limits: Easy, algorithmic step.
agent_relevance: Model-building from text is reliable for reasoning models; the cost is in the combinatorial steps.

source: Rodler (2023) Don't Treat the Symptom, Find the Cause! Efficient AI Methods for (Interactive) Debugging (habilitation thesis)
finding: Thesis summarising HS-Tree (Reiter 1987, breadth-first, node- and edge-labelled tree) and the author's improvements. HS-Tree is sound, complete and best-first; it can be stopped any time and still returns the diagnoses found so far. Non-minimal diagnoses and duplicate paths are closed without any theorem prover call.
numbers: HS-Tree needs O(|Sol_HS| + |COMPS| x n_C) consistency checks, where n_C is the number of computed minimal conflicts. The theorem prover calls inside conflict computation (QuickXplain) are the main cost.
quote: the execution of HS-Tree can be stopped at any point in time
limits: Author's own summary of own work.
agent_relevance: The anytime property fits a thinking loop with a budget: stop the search, keep the diagnoses found.

source: Rodler (2022) DynamicHS (in thesis 2306.12850, section 3.1.2)
finding: DynamicHS keeps state across a sequential diagnosis session and avoids repeated work done by plain HS-Tree. The same diagnoses are returned.
numbers: DynamicHS faster than HS-Tree in 99.4% of tested scenarios; median runtime saving 52%, maximal 75% (HS-Tree up to about 4x the time on average); in single sessions HS-Tree took more than 9x as long.
limits: Real-world ontology and knowledge-base benchmarks; costs more memory.
agent_relevance: If the agent re-runs hitting-set search after each new observation, keep the tree and conflicts instead of restarting.

source: Rodler (2022) RBF-HS / HBF-HS (in thesis 2306.12850)
finding: Recursive best-first hitting set search (RBF-HS) gives linear-space best-first diagnosis computation. HS-Tree is the baseline.
numbers: RBF-HS cut memory by up to several orders of magnitude; one case with 65% runtime saving and 99.9% memory reduction; one case where HS-Tree ran out of 32 GB while RBF-HS stored at most 125 nodes. For probability-ordered diagnoses, memory saved roughly one-to-one against runtime overhead; HBF-HS is the compromise.
limits: Real-world benchmarks; trade-off runtime versus memory.
agent_relevance: Context-window-like memory limits make linear-space search relevant for an agent.

source: Rodler (2023) thesis - sequential diagnosis and queries
finding: After HS-Tree yields many candidate diagnoses, queries to an oracle (tests, probes, expert questions) are chosen so each answer rules out candidates. Query choice uses information-theoretic heuristics.
numbers: Qualitative description of sequential diagnosis and discriminating queries.
limits: Review of the author's work; no new experiments here.
agent_relevance: This is the loop shape for an agent: hypothesise suspects, pick the test that splits them, update, repeat.

source: Shchekotykhin, Friedrich, Fleiss, Rodler (2011/2014) Interactive ontology debugging: two query strategies for efficient fault localization
finding: Diagnoses from HS-Tree are narrowed by yes/no queries to an oracle. Entropy-based query selection beat split-in-half and helped even with equal fault probabilities.
numbers: Abstract: entropy-based method significantly reduces the number of queries versus split-in-half, even when all fault probabilities are equal. Table numbers not extracted.
quote: superiority of entropy-based query selection even in cases where all fault probabilities are equal
limits: Ontology debugging; simulated oracle.
agent_relevance: Entropy-based choice of the next probe is a direct design rule for the agent's test selection.

source: Shchekotykhin, Friedrich, Rodler, Fleiss (2012) Direct computation of diagnoses for ontology debugging (Inv-HS-Tree)
finding: Inv-HS-Tree computes diagnoses directly with Inv-QuickXplain, with no need to precompute minimal conflicts. Reiter's HS-Tree needs one conflict per tree node, which is costly when there are many conflicts.
numbers: In 13 hard ontology cases HS-Tree could not find all requested diagnoses within 2 hours; e.g. csa-conference-ekaw gave only 1 diagnosis, ldoa-conference-confof 1 and 9. Inv-HS-Tree found one minimal diagnosis in about 25 seconds on average. Tests on 146 ontologies asking for 1, 9 and 30 diagnoses. Anatomy ontologies had 11545 and 4838 axioms.
limits: Description-logic reasoner cost dominates; 2-hour limit.
agent_relevance: Conflict-first search is expensive when conflicts are many. The alternative is to grow a diagnosis directly and check it.

source: Ielo, Mazzotta, Penaloza, Ricca (2024) Enumerating Minimal Unsatisfiable Cores of LTLf formulas
finding: Enumerates all minimal unsatisfiable cores (conflicts) of LTLf specifications, with mus2muc compared with ReMUS, MARCO and BinaryMUC. MARCO-style enumeration uses minimal hitting-set dualisation.
numbers: Benchmark suite has 2079 unsatisfiable instances from 15 applications; 300 s timeout; hardest instances are not fully enumerated within the timeout.
limits: Specification formulas, not LLM text; timeouts leave incomplete enumeration.
agent_relevance: Conflict enumeration is a real bottleneck even with modern solvers. Anytime partial enumeration is the norm.

source: Paul, Yu, Dekker, Ignatiev, Stuckey (2024) Formal Explanations for Neuro-Symbolic AI
finding: Explains neuro-symbolic decisions by computing a formal explanation of the symbolic part first (via minimal unsatisfiable subsets), then the neural part. Reference list includes hitting-set dualisation MUS extraction.
numbers: No hitting-set experiment values extracted; cites Ignatiev et al., Smallest MUS Extraction with Minimal Hitting Set Dualization (2015).
limits: Not an LLM diagnosis paper.
agent_relevance: Shows conflict/diagnosis duality is used to explain neural pipelines.

source: Roy et al. (2024) Exploring LLM-based Agents for Root Cause Analysis (Microsoft)
finding: A ReAct agent with retrieval tools was tested on production cloud incidents. It matched strong baselines on correctness but with far fewer hallucinations. Adding discussion threads as inputs gave no significant gain. No hitting-set method was used.
numbers: Correct predictions: CoT 39%, ReAct S+Q BM25 35%; 28 of 97 solved by all three models. Hallucination rate: ReAct 4% vs CoT 12% vs retrieval baseline RB(k=10) 40%. Among wrong predictions, hallucination in 49% (29/59) for RB(k=10), 18% (11/59) for CoT and 6% (4/63) for ReAct. Among correct RB(k=10) predictions 26% (10/38).
quote: ReAct performs competitively with strong retrieval and reasoning baselines, but with highly increased factual accuracy
limits: Single company dataset; lexical metrics poor. Single-candidate answers, not set-valued.
agent_relevance: Tool-grounded loops cut hallucination but not accuracy; evidence retrieval alone does not give diagnosis. A candidate-set search is missing here.

source: Xu et al. (2025) OpenRCA: Can LLMs Locate the Root Cause of Software Failures? (ICLR 2025)
finding: Benchmark of 335 failures with 68.5 GB telemetry from three enterprise systems. The best model solved a small share even with the RCA-agent scaffold.
numbers: Claude 3.5 Sonnet with RCA-agent: 11.34% accuracy. A case counts as right only if all root-cause elements (time, component, reason) match.
limits: Strict all-elements match; telemetry very large.
agent_relevance: Baseline of an agent with no systematic suspect-set search. Set-valued answers are scored strictly.

source: Kim, Park, Yun, Lee (2026) Why Do AI Agents Systematically Fail at Cloud Root Cause Analysis?
finding: Ran full OpenRCA with five LLMs (1675 agent runs). Perfect-accuracy rates were 3.9% to 12.5%. Failures were shared across models, so the cause is the agent framework, not the model.
numbers: Hallucination in interpretation in 71.2% of runs; Incomplete Exploration 63.9%; Symptom-as-Cause 39.9% (above 45% for GPT-5 mini and GPT-OSS 120B); No Cross-Validation 18.6%; max step exhaustion 4.1%.
limits: Observational pitfall coding; one benchmark.
agent_relevance: Incomplete exploration and symptom-as-cause are exactly the failures a hitting-set tree prevents: it forces coverage of alternatives and separates symptoms from minimal causes.

source: Kim et al. (2026) mitigation experiments (2602.09937)
finding: Prompt fixes did not work. Hypothesis-driven prompting (explicit hypothesis per KPI category) widened coverage but did not suppress interpretation errors; pitfall-aware prompting gave no meaningful gain. Structural change did help.
numbers: Prompt tests on Claude Sonnet 4 across 70 Bank-domain tasks. Richer inter-agent protocol with code and execution output cut communication pitfalls by up to 15 percentage points (about 14 pp for GPT-5 mini, 15 pp for Claude Sonnet 4), improved detection scores for all models and cut execution time by 22.3% (steps per run 11.9 to 9.2, -22.1%).
limits: Small tasks; one model for prompt tests.
agent_relevance: Supports putting structure in the scaffold (explicit hypothesis list and checks), not only in prompt wording.

source: Fang et al. (2026) OpenRCA 2.0: From Outcome Labels to Causal Process Supervision
finding: Adds step-wise causal annotation. Across 11 frontier LLMs, exact recovery of the root-cause set is rare; naming one correct service is far more common than a verified causal path.
numbers: Exact Match 20.7%, pair-level F1 34.1%; verified causal path reachability 61.5%; at least one correct root-cause service 76.0% (from search summary; gap of 14.5 pp to path reachability in paper text).
limits: Single benchmark; fault injection on microservice systems.
agent_relevance: Models find a suspect but not the full minimal set: a set-completeness check is the missing piece. Hitting-set minimality gives a precise test.

source: Reiter (1987) A theory of diagnosis from first principles. Artificial Intelligence 32
finding: Founding paper. Diagnoses are minimal hitting sets of the collection of conflict sets. HS-tree builds this breadth-first, reusing conflicts and pruning.
numbers: Not opened. The theorem is restated in several opened sources (Rodler thesis; DX 2025; 1209.0997).
limits: Original pruning had a flaw later corrected by Greiner et al.
agent_relevance: The core definition for suspect search: a set of components that touches every conflict.

source: Greiner, Smith, Wilkerson (1989) A correction to the algorithm in Reiter's theory of diagnosis. Artif. Intell. 41
finding: Background knowledge, not opened: Reiter's pruning could lose minimal diagnoses when conflicts are not minimal; the fix is the HS-DAG that reuses nodes (a DAG, not a tree).
numbers: Not opened; no figures taken.
limits: Described from general literature knowledge, not verified this session.
agent_relevance: Our agent's conflicts will often be non-minimal (LLM-written), so the DAG fix is the relevant version.

source: de Kleer and Williams (1987) Diagnosing multiple faults. Artif. Intell. 32 (GDE)
finding: GDE computes conflicts with an ATMS and candidates from them, in parallel with Reiter. Not opened.
numbers: Not opened.
limits: Not verified this session.
agent_relevance: Parallel line of the same idea; adds probabilities to choose the next measurement.

source: Stern, Puzis, Felner et al. (2012) Exploring the Duality in Conflict-Directed Model-Based Diagnosis (AAAI)
finding: Search snippet only: exploits the duality between conflicts and diagnoses to extend Reiter's theory. Not opened.
numbers: Not opened; no numbers.
limits: Snippet-level.
agent_relevance: Possible route to generate diagnoses and conflicts in alternation.

source: Feldman, Provan, van Gemund (2010) SAFARI stochastic diagnosis
finding: Search snippet: SAFARI trades completeness for efficiency when computing multiple minimal-cardinality diagnoses on 74XXX/ISCAS85 circuits. Not opened.
numbers: Not opened.
limits: Snippet-level.
agent_relevance: Incomplete but fast sampling may suit an LLM agent with a budget.

source: Abreu et al. (2010) Simultaneous debugging of software faults (SIR-M)
finding: Search snippet: extended the SIR benchmark to multiple faults and ranks multiple-fault diagnoses by probability. Not opened.
numbers: Not opened.
limits: Snippet-level.
agent_relevance: Candidate ground truth for multi-fault tests of an agent.

source: SafeMin: Large Language Models for Safe Minimization (ICSE 2025)
finding: Search snippet only: an LLM and an SMT solver together compute minimal unsatisfiable subsets; the solver guards against LLM hallucination. Not opened.
numbers: Snippet: 42.1% more non-unique MUSes found than without the LLM macro-reasoning step, on LeetCode string benchmarks.
limits: Snippet-level; figure not verified.
agent_relevance: Closest example of LLM-in-the-loop conflict (MUS) minimisation with a checker, the pattern we want.

source: Xu et al. (2026) Delta1 with LLM: symbolic and neural integration for credible and explainable reasoning
finding: Pipeline builds minimal unsatisfiable clause sets deterministically and uses an LLM only to turn proofs into natural language. Only the first page was read.
numbers: Case studies in health care, compliance, regulatory conformance and contract analysis; no accuracy figure read.
limits: Only abstract and first page checked.
agent_relevance: Division of labour: solver does minimal sets, LLM only explains.

source: Search finding: no study found placing an LLM inside Reiter HS-tree or HS-DAG
finding: After 8 web searches and several fetches, no 2020-2026 study was found that puts an LLM inside a hitting-set tree, or tests LLMs on HS-DAG non-minimal conflict handling. The DX 2025 paper is the closest. This is a gap, not a negative result.
numbers: 0 direct studies found. Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and arXiv API calls returned rate-limit errors (429), so the search was not exhaustive.
limits: Absence of evidence under a limited search.
agent_relevance: Our agent would be a novel use; expect to measure it ourselves.
